newsitem.title: QATAR: Committe to discuss Qatar-Bahrain dispute on Sunday.
newsitem.headline: Committe to discuss Qatar-Bahrain dispute on Sunday.

text.p: Foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman and the United Arab Emirates are expected to meet Qatari leaders on Sunday to narrow differences over a territorial dispute with Manama, a Qatari official said.

"The meeting in Doha is being held under the auspices of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) to seek ways of narrowing the differences between the two council members," the official told Reuters on Saturday.

The four-state mediation committee set up by a GCC summit in Doha in December met twice in Riyadh this month, but failed to pursuade the two countries to agree to a memorandum of understanding between them. It decided to visit the two Gulf states to continue its mediation efforts.
The official said Bahrain's foreign minister will not attend Sunday's meeting.
"The committee will leave for Manama after its mission in Doha to hold separate talks with Bahraini leaders," he added.
Qatar's Foreign Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani said earlier that both countries had objected to different points in the seven-point document.
But Bahrain's Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammad Bin Mubarak al-Khalifa said Manama had informed the committee that it had welcomed the memorandum.
Qatar and Bahrain have been locked for decades in a dispute over a cluster of islands, sandbanks and reefs in the Gulf, controlled by Manama since the 1930s, but also claimed by Doha.
Doha took the territorial dispute to the International Court of Justice at the Hague in 1991, a move opposed by Manama which insists on a regional solution.

Ties were further strained after Bahrain accused two Qataris of spying -- which Doha denied -- and boycotted the Gulf Cooperation Council's December summit in Qatar. Bahrain later pardoned the two Qataris.
